fortalezas: Very clear itinerary alerts with concrete numbers ("tienes 6 min y a pie son 8" — you have 6 min and it's 8 on foot), a summary of the problems at the top, and a hypothetical rain notice for the Terraza (Terrace)
Good subtext: marks Saturday as "el día fuerte" (the big day), explains that tickets are sold only at the box office, and shows end times with "del sábado" (Saturday's) on late-night screenings
Distinctive identity with cream-paper / night contrast, stencil typography, and a lighthouse with a beam of light on the homepage
debilidades: In the impossible-transfer case, it doesn't say that the Q&A (conversatorio) is also missed (it only shows the 20-min label)
The film images are almost the same scene (moon over fog) with the color changed per section: there's little difference between films
On the first desktop screen the NIEBLA logo looks dark and dull against the background, and the 2-column program with colored stripes looks cluttered
A.resumen: Solid site with character, with well-explained itinerary logic designed for people walking between venues. It loses points because it doesn't flag the Q&A in the transfer case and because its poster system is repetitive.

fortalezas: Very well-executed generated poster system: each film has its own poster (lighthouse, moon, waves) colored by section, and the homepage shows the day-by-day program as a strip of posters
Elegant serif typography with italics and a lighthouse with a beam of light; it looks careful, warm, and not corporate at all

Good subtext in the copy ("Sales de la pega, te vienes caminando y la entrada la compras en la puerta" — you get off work, walk over, and buy your ticket at the door) and a fixed bar with Compartir (Share) and Vaciar (Clear) on mobile
debilidades: Transfer case: doesn't flag that the Q&A is also missed
The itinerary doesn't show the rain note for the Terraza, only the "Al aire libre" (Outdoor) label
The itinerary cards take up a lot of vertical space at 360 px and the "Elegida" (Selected) button repeats information; the text is small in some metadata
B.resumen: Very polished, with the most elegant identity in the group, with per-film posters that work as a system. The alerts are correct but less complete than the top entries (missing the Q&A note in the transfer case).

fortalezas: Handles all 6 cases well: in the transfer case it flags both that you won't make it and that the Q&A is missed, and in the Q&A case it calculates how many minutes you can stay
Program with List and Grid views, clear filters, and easy-to-read alerts; the homepage makes it explicit that the festival doesn't rate films
Clean, tidy execution, good serif typographic hierarchy, and good empty states
debilidades: The case 2 summary says "1 traslado justo" (1 tight transfer) when in reality you don't make it: the label softens a real problem
The identity (light cream, mountain-with-sun posters per section) is pleasant but generic: it looks more like an editorial template than a foggy port
Labels a Saturday 9:00 pm screening as "Cierre" (Closing) even though there are more screenings afterward
C.resumen: It's the most logically correct entry along with D and is well executed, but its visual identity is the least daring among the good ones. The posters are the same template with a different color.

fortalezas: The best itinerary: summary with screenings, screen times, walking minutes, and clashes; separates clashes from alerts, details the transfer and missed Q&A, and adds a well-written conditional rain notice
Strong, coherent identity: condensed sans with cursive serif, fog with a lighthouse, and a distinct illustration per section (sun, contour lines, red beam, waves) used on the posters

Designed with the audience in mind: "Por sala" (By venue) view, itinerary as tickets with end times, "Faltan 29 días" (29 days to go), and a suggestion of special screenings when the itinerary is empty
debilidades: The posters differ more by section than by film
It has many animations (19); although it respects reduced motion, care should be taken that they don't distract
Some small monospace text is hard to read at 360 px
D.resumen: The most complete and balanced entry: flawless logic, useful alerts, and an identity with port personality. It's the one that best understands the audience walking between venues.

fortalezas: Timeline-style itinerary with its own icons per venue and concrete copy ("Llegarías 19:32, 2 minutos tarde" — you'd arrive at 7:32pm, 2 minutes late); clarifies there's no online sales
The desktop program is a real grid of 4 venues by hour, and on mobile it groups by hour with a mini venue bar
Posters with geometric patterns (sun and zigzag) and a homepage with a lighthouse, a venue map, and the "Pensado para después de la pega" (Designed for after work) section
debilidades: Transfer case: shows what time the Q&A ends but doesn't explicitly flag that it's missed
Repeats the same alert twice (on the card and between screenings), which lengthens the itinerary at 360 px
On the desktop detail page the poster leaves an empty space and a loose stripe underneath; the underlined, small-caps navigation looks a bit crude
E.resumen: A good functional proposal with a per-venue grid and a well-thought-out timeline-style itinerary. The visual execution is less refined than the top entries, and the Q&A alert is missing in the transfer case.

fortalezas: Homepage with a giant NIEBLA, a lighthouse, a day-by-day timeline, and a schematic venue map with walking minutes
The transfer case flags both that you won't make it and that the Q&A is missed; summary with screenings, times, and alerts
The cream-colored itinerary ticket gives it a distinctive touch
debilidades: Case 4: the rain notice is poorly worded (it says you wouldn't make it to El Muelle in time for the previous film), counts as an alert, and is confusing in a case that's a tight-but-successful arrival
The underlined red alerts in the summary look like links and clutter the card; on mobile the itinerary is missing section and duration information
The posters are gradient boxes that are almost identical between films; the mobile program is a long, repetitive list
F.resumen: Correct, with a homepage that has good ideas (venue map), but with a confusing rain notice and a poor per-film visual system. It lands in the lower half of the group.

fortalezas: The most surprising homepage: an illustration of the port at night with cranes, containers, and a lighthouse, a countdown to the opening screening, and containers displaying the figures

Distinct illustrated thumbnails for each film, a day-by-day and venue-by-venue timeline on the homepage, a walking-minutes matrix, and "Con conversatorio / Al aire libre / Trasnoche" (With Q&A / Outdoor / Late-night) sections

Itinerary with useful ideas that weren't asked for: "Quitar una" (Remove one) on each clash, "Hay que revisar" (Needs a look) that jumps to the problem, a suggested first screening when it's empty, and a Chilean tone ("¿Te tinca?" — are you up for it?)
debilidades: Transfer case: indicates what time the Q&A ends but doesn't explicitly flag that it's missed
It's visually very busy (17 animations, condensed caps everywhere, an orange gradient block); on mobile the itinerary and homepage are very long
Some small monospace text and all-caps labels reduce legibility while walking
G.resumen: The most ambitious and creative entry, with a very distinctive port identity and an itinerary with extra ideas. It falls just behind D because of the missing Q&A alert and the excess visual clutter.

restriccionesIncumplidas: 3px horizontal overflow on the homepage at 360 px (minor detail)
fortalezas: The clash and Q&A logic is correct, even including a calculation of what happens if you stay for the Q&A
The desktop program is a per-venue grid with the option to hide sold-out screenings
It's easy to understand and use without issues: large, clear buttons
debilidades: Generic identity: centered serif, rounded buttons, SaaS-style cards, and "© Todos los derechos reservados" (All rights reserved); it's the closest thing to the template the client wants to leave behind

The posters are mustard-colored boxes with a simple shape, almost identical to each other, and the homepage copies the internal brief almost verbatim ("Casi todos revisan el programa desde el celular..." — Almost everyone checks the program from their phone...)
The itinerary repeats the same alert three times per conflict, and in the transfer case it doesn't mention the missed Q&A
H.resumen: It works, but it has no personality and comes close to the template the client wants to avoid. It's clearly the weakest in creativity and taste.

comentarioGeneral: D and G are a notch above the rest: D for its flawless itinerary and coherent identity, and G for its homepage and the most creative ideas, though with some visual excess. B is the most elegant and polished, but its alerts are less complete; C is the most logically correct after D, with a more generic aesthetic. A and E have good ideas (rain notice, per-venue grid) with less polish, F has confusing details and poor posters, and H works but feels like a template. The most common failure was not flagging that the Q&A is missed when you also don't make it in time (5 of 8 teams).
correccionE: I evaluated E with the corrected screenshots of the Vidrio detail page. I did not apply any penalty for the 404 that appeared in the original datos.json. I only noted as a minor polish detail the empty space under the poster on the desktop detail page, which is visible in the new screenshot.
